Wilderness of Paran
PAY-ran
proper noun (place)
Hebrew Paran; a large wilderness south of Canaan from which the twelve spies were sent into the promised land.

📖 Biblical Definition

The wilderness of Paran was a large desert region south of Canaan, in the Sinai peninsula, where Israel encamped during the wilderness years and from which the twelve spies were sent to search out the promised land. After leaving Sinai, "the children of Israel took their journeys... and the cloud rested in the wilderness of Paran" (Num 10:12). From Paran, at Kadesh, "Moses by the commandment of the LORD sent" the twelve men to spy out Canaan (Num 13:3, 26); and it was to Paran they returned with their report, ten of them bringing an evil report that provoked the people's unbelief and the forty years of wandering. Paran had earlier been the dwelling-place of Ishmael, who "dwelt in the wilderness of Paran" after he and Hagar were sent away (Gen 21:21). Long after, David withdrew to the wilderness of Paran at the death of Samuel (1 Sam 25:1). Paran stands in the dictionary as the wilderness of the spies and of unbelief, the place from which Israel looked into the land of promise and turned back in fear, a solemn witness that the borders of blessing may be reached and yet forfeited by unbelief, and that the report we believe — the faith of Caleb and Joshua or the fear of the ten — determines whether we enter the rest of God.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A large wilderness south of Canaan (Num 10:12; 13:3) from which the twelve spies were sent into the promised land; the place of Israel's unbelief at the spies' evil report, and earlier the dwelling of Ishmael.

WILDERNESS OF PARAN, proper noun. A large desert region south of Canaan.

Where the cloud rested after Israel left Sinai (Num 10:12).

From which (at Kadesh) the twelve spies were sent into Canaan (Num 13:3, 26).

Where the ten spies' evil report provoked Israel's unbelief.

Earlier the dwelling of Ishmael (Gen 21:21); later a refuge of David (1 Sam 25:1).

📖 Key Scripture

Num 10:12 — "And the children of Israel took their journeys out of the wilderness of Sinai; and the cloud rested in the wilderness of Paran."

Num 13:3 — "And Moses by the commandment of the LORD sent them from the wilderness of Paran: all those men were heads of the children of Israel."

Num 13:26 — "And they went and came to Moses, and to Aaron, and to all the congregation of the children of Israel, unto the wilderness of Paran, to Kadesh..."

Heb 3:19 — "So we see that they could not enter in because of unbelief."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Paran needs no defense from redefinition; its lesson is that the borders of blessing may be reached and yet forfeited through unbelief, while faith enters into the rest of God.

expand to see more

Unbelief-at-the-border correction. From Paran, Israel stood at the very threshold of the promised land, sent the spies, and then turned back in fear at the evil report of the ten. The dictionary holds the sobering lesson of Hebrews: "they could not enter in because of unbelief" (Heb 3:19). It is possible to come near the blessing of God and forfeit it through fear and distrust; the borders of Canaan are reached by many who never enter, because they believe the report of fear rather than the promise of God.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the power of the report we believe. Twelve men saw the same land; two believed God and were ready to go up, ten saw only giants and walled cities. The dictionary commends the faith of Caleb and Joshua: faith reckons with the promise and power of God, not merely with the visible obstacles, and those who believe the good report — that the LORD is able to bring His people in — enter the rest that unbelief forfeits.
